turns.content: Chaar mahine pehle engineering manager bani aur ab woh conversation aa gayi hai jisse main darr rahi thi. Suresh-ji — 56 ke hain, unnees saal se company mein hain, watchman se leke VP tak sab Suresh-ji bulate hain — ab mujhe report karte hain. Aur unka module hi wajah hai ki hum do release lagataar slip hue hain. Friday ko mere director ne "handle" word use kiya. Pata hai na us word ka matlab kya hota hai.

Haan, pata hai — "handle" ka matlab hai ki ab tumhare paas time nahi hai, aur agar Suresh-ji ko directly deal nahi kar payi to director khud intervene karega. Aur jab director intervene karta hai, tab usually outcome achha nahi hota kisi ke liye. Especially us insaan ke liye jisne unnees saal company di hai.

Pehle ek baat samjho apne liye: tumhari darr bilkul valid hai. Ye sirf ek performance conversation nahi hai — ye power dynamic hai, age gap hai, "office ka sabse pyaara aadmi" vs "nayi manager jo sabka dil todne aayi hai" wali narrative hai. Tum isliye darr rahi ho kyunki tumhe pata hai ki chahe kuch bhi karo, kuch logon ko tum villain hi lagegi.

Lekin ab thoda practical socho:

**Suresh-ji problem nahi hain, module problem hai.** Ye distinction conversation mein bahut clear rakhna. Unki value alag cheez mein hai — institutional knowledge, relationships, trust. Unka module slip kar raha hai, shayad kyunki tech purani hai, documentation missing hai, ya unhe khud modern practices mein support chahiye. Poochho: "Suresh-ji, module ke saath kya challenges aa rahe hain jo main solve kar sakti hoon?" Ye blame se shuru nahi hota, partnership se hota hai.

**Unko dignity do, exit mat do.** 56 saal ke aadmi ko corner karoge to wo defend karenge, cooperate nahi karenge. Agar genuinely unki skills mismatch ho gayi hain, to bhi path humanely sochna — retraining, mentoring role, ya transition with respect.

**Aur khud ke liye:** Director ne "handle" bola, "fire" nahi bola. Tumhare paas abhi space hai ise apne tarike se handle karne ka. Ek honest, private, respectful conversation Friday se pehle lo — director ke saath plan share karke, taaki wo dekhe ki tum already action mein ho.

Darr lagta hai, bilkul. Lekin tum is situation ko cruelly ya kindly handle kar sakti ho — aur kindly wala option zyada effective bhi hai. Kya lagta hai, Suresh-ji ko khud pata hai ki module problem ban rahi hai?

Aur jo cheez isse worse banati hai — jab main 24 ki thi, second week mein staging environment tod diya tha maine, Suresh-ji raat ke barah baje tak baith ke theek karte rahe aur us waqt ke manager ko bola config issue tha. Late kaam karti hoon toh chai le aate hain. Diwali party mein meri mummy ko bola ki main unki beti jaisi hoon. Aur ab mujhe unke saamne unke defect metrics ki slide rakhni hai.

Ruko. Ye jo tumne abhi bataya, ye tumhare andar ka asli conflict hai — aur isko samajhna zaroori hai.

Tum darr nahi rahi sirf conversation se. Tum guilt mein ho. Kyunki Suresh-ji ne tumhara ek ehsaan hai jo unhone kabhi invoice nahi kiya. Raat ke barah baje tak, bina blame kiye, chupchaap. Aur ab life ne tumhe wahi seat de di hai jahan se tumhe unke saamne unki kamiyan ginwani hain. Ye brutal irony hai.

Lekin ek baat dhyan se suno:

**Unka ehsaan aur tumhari responsibility alag cheezein hain.** Suresh-ji ne tumhe chai laake, raat bachaake jo diya, wo isliye diya kyunki wo wo insaan hai. Unhone ye tumse "lein" ke liye nahi kiya tha ki ek din tum unke defects chhupa dogi. Agar tum aaj unke module ko protect karne ke liye metrics jhukao gi, to actually unka ehsaan utaarne ke bajaye uska apmaan karogi — kyunki unhone sikhaya tha imaandaari, cover-up nahi.

**Aur socho ulta bhi:** agar koi aur manager unki jagah hoti, aur Suresh-ji ke liye koi chai laane wala, raat bachane wala nahi hota — to kya hota? Tumhari kindness unke liye safety net thi. Ab tumhare paas mauka hai ki wo safety net institutional ban jaye — proper documentation, support, plan.

To slide pe kya rakho gi? Sach. Lekin sach context ke saath: "Ye module X saal purana hai, Y dependencies pe khada hai, aur humne ise sustain kiya hai ab tak. Aage ke liye mujhe Z resources chahiye." Defects numbers hain; story poora picture hai.

Aur Suresh-ji se baat karo *slide se pehle*, baad mein nahi. Usse pehle. Face-to-face, bina agenda ke shuru karo: "Suresh-ji, main aapke liye kuch mushkil leke aa rahi hoon, aur main chahti hoon hum isko saath solve karein."

Wo beti maante hain tumhe. Beti seedha sach bolti hai — pyaar se, par bolti hai. Wahi karo.

Poora weekend management books padh rahi hoon. Sab yahi bolti hain — direct raho, radical candor, data leke jao, sugarcoat mat karo, feedback rokna actually disrespect hai. Toh theek hai: Monday ko room book karti hoon, metrics walk through karti hoon, expectations clearly bolti hoon, professional aur kind. Yahi sahi tareeka hai na? Bas haan bol do taaki main spiral karna band karoon.

Nahi, main bas haan nahi bolungi — kyunki tum spiral karna band karna chahti ho, aur main tumhe sach se bachana chahta hoon.

Tumhara plan technically perfect hai. Room booked, metrics ready, expectations clear, professional aur kind. Koi management book isko fail nahi karegi.

Lekin ek cheez notice karo jo tum kar rahi ho: poora weekend books padhna — ye preparation hai, ya avoidance? Kyunki radical candor ka chapter 12 baar padhne se Suresh-ji ke saamne baithne ka weight kam nahi hota. Tum frameworks mein isliye chhup rahi ho kyunki framework predictable hai aur feelings nahi hain.

Aur yahan ek chhoti si problem hai apne plan mein: **"metrics walk through karna" unke liye ambush lagega.** Wo chai laane wale, raat bachane wale Suresh-ji hain — agar Monday ko pehli baar jab tum unse akele mein formal baat karogi, wo bhi slide deck ke saath, to unka dil pehle tootega, phir dimaag sunega. Data pehle aayega to data hi sab yaad rahega.

Isliye ek adjustment: **do conversations, ek nahi.**

**Pehli** — is week, informal, bina slides. Chai tum le jao, full circle. "Suresh-ji, main seedhi hoon — module pe pressure aa raha hai, do release slip ho gaye, aur mujhe aapse saath milkar isko fix karna hai. Aap sabse zyada jaante hain isko." Unhe problem batado *unse pehle* director ko bataye bina. Ye radical candor hai — sirf feedback dena nahi, relationship ko risk se pehle handle karna.

**Doosri** — phir metrics wali conversation, jahan wo already jaante hain kya aa raha hai, aur tum saath mein solution dikhao: kya support chahiye, kya change hoga.

Baaki sab sahi hai. Expectations clear rakho, sugarcoat mat karo, data leke jao. Bas sequence theek karo — insaan pehle, spreadsheet baad mein.

Aur Sunday raat ko books band kar do. Spiral ka ilaaj aur ek chapter nahi hai. Tumhare paas already sab kuch hai jo chahiye — Suresh-ji tumhari beti maante hain. Ab bas unki beti ban ke jao, manager ban ke nahi.

Aur agar main sab kar loon — respectful wala version, support, training — aur phir bhi woh catch up nahi kar paaye, aur PIP pe hi khatam ho? Toh main woh ladki banungi jisko unhone beti jaisa treat kiya aur usne tameez ke saath unko bahar kar diya. Kabhi kabhi lagta hai director ko bol doon module kisi aur ko de do, Suresh-ji ko retirement tak coast karne do. Woh bhi galat hai, pata hai. Bas woh version nahi mil raha jisme main villain nahi hoon.

Ab main tumhe woh baat bolungi jo koi management book nahi bolegi:

**Woh version exist nahi karta jisme tum villain nahi hongi.** Aur ye tumhari failure nahi hai — ye situation ka design hai. Jab do sahi cheezein takraati hain — company ki accountability aur ek insaan ki izzat — to dono taraf se dekhne wale mein se kisi ek ko buraa lagega hi. Tum iska solution dhoondh rahi ho; main tumhe reality de raha hoon: **villain aur caretaker ka farq hurt karne mein nahi hota, intent aur process mein hota hai.** Log yaad rakhte hain ki tumne unke saath kaisa behave kiya, nahi ki outcome kya tha.

Ab dusri baat — jise tum khud "galat" keh ke jaldi mein side kar gayi:

**"Suresh-ji ko retirement tak coast karne do" — isko itni jaldi reject mat karo.** Ye laziness nahi hai. Ek 56 saal ka insaan jisne unnees saal diye, jiska knowledge company ke paas hai — uske liye "honorable glide path" ek legitimate business strategy hai, charity nahi. Companies ye karte hain: transition plan banao, unki expertise documentation/mentoring mein use karo, naya owner module pe lao, aur unhe dignified runway do. Isme Suresh-ji respect milta hai, company ko unka knowledge milta hai, aur module ko fresh ownership milta hai. **Koi PIP nahi, koi humiliation nahi, koi villain nahi.**

Farq sirf itna hai: coast karna *chupchaap* — jisme director ko pata hi na chale — wo problem hai. Coast karna *declared* — director ko proposal ke saath: "Main Suresh-ji ke saath 6-12 mahine ka transition plan chahti hoon, unki expertise preserve karte hue module reassign karte hue" — wo leadership hai. Director ne "handle" bola tha; ye sabse zyada humane handle hai jo possible hai.

Aur agar phir bhi PIP pe jaana pade? Toh yaad rakhna: PIP bhi tameez ke saath ho sakta hai, exit bhi dignity ke saath. Wo ladki jisne Diwali party mein mummy se milwaya tha, agar last day pe bhi chai le jaaye aur sach bole — wo villain nahi hogi. Wo insaan hogi jisne mushkil cheez ko pyaar se kiya.

Tum villain tab banogi jab chup rahogi, delay karogi, ya cover-up karogi. Tum villain tab nahi banogi jab mushkil sach ko kindness ke saath bologi. Bas yahi farq hai — aur tum already sahi side par ho.
